messages.Server:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 11

Hello Babti

events.title: Create a socket
events.what: The server app creates a socket object.
events.why: A socket is how an app asks the OS to connect, send, or read bytes.

events.title: Reserve the server port
events.what: The server claims port 8080 on its own IP address.
events.why: A port tells the OS which network endpoint should get incoming traffic.

events.title: Start listening
events.what: The server tells its OS to accept new connections on port 8080.
events.why: A listening socket waits for clients. The OS queues finished connections for Accept().

events.title: Open the URL
events.what: The browser opens the address for /hello on port 8080.
events.why: The IP address identifies the server and /hello is the resource the browser wants.

events.title: Build the HTTP request
events.what: The browser writes a GET request as bytes.
events.why: GET asks for a resource. The Host line names the server and a blank line ends the headers.

events.title: Create a socket
events.what: The browser creates a socket object.
events.why: A socket is how an app asks the OS to connect, send, or read bytes.

events.title: Ask the kernel to connect
events.what: The browser asks the OS to open a TCP connection to the server.
events.why: Connect() starts the handshake. The HTTP request is already in memory.

events.title: Choose a local port
events.what: Assigned local port 51000.
events.why: The client uses its own port so replies can find this connection.

events.title: Update TCP state
events.what: Client changes its TCP state to SYN sent.
events.why: The client has started the handshake and is waiting for SYN+ACK.

events.title: Create a TCP segment
events.what: Client makes a SYN control segment.
events.why: SYN starts the handshake and tells the server the client’s starting sequence number.

events.title: Look up the next hop
events.what: Next stop is 192.0.2.1.
events.why: A route picks the next stop. The IP destination stays the final computer.

events.title: Wrap the segment in IPv4
events.what: IPv4 wraps the TCP segment in a 40-byte packet.
events.why: TCP supplies the ports. IPv4 adds the source IP, destination IP, and TTL.

events.title: Look up the next hop
events.what: Next stop is 198.51.100.20.
events.why: A route picks the next stop. The IP destination stays the final computer.

events.title: Forward the packet
events.what: The router forwards the packet and lowers TTL to 63.
events.why: TTL is the packet’s hop budget. Lowering it at each router keeps packets from looping forever.

events.title: Hand the segment to TCP
events.raw: [Server] Ipv4.UnwrapPacket protocol=6 -> deliver enclosed segment to TCP
events.what: Server opens the IPv4 packet and takes out the TCP segment.
events.why: Protocol number 6 tells IPv4 that the payload belongs to TCP.

events.title: Match the listening socket
events.raw: [Server kernel] SYN matched listening socket at 198.51.100.20:8080
events.what: The server OS finds its listener on port 8080.
events.why: The first SYN makes the OS create TCP state for this specific client.

events.title: Process the incoming segment
events.what: Server TCP reads the ports, flags, and sequence numbers.
events.why: TCP uses control flags and sequence numbers to update the connection.

events.title: Update TCP state
events.what: Server changes its TCP state to SYN received.
events.why: The server has received SYN and will wait for the final ACK.

events.title: Create a TCP segment
events.what: Server makes a SYN+ACK control segment.
events.why: The server acknowledges the client’s SYN and sends its own starting sequence number.

events.title: Look up the next hop
events.what: Next stop is 198.51.100.1.
events.why: A route picks the next stop. The IP destination stays the final computer.

events.title: Wrap the segment in IPv4
events.what: IPv4 wraps the TCP segment in a 40-byte packet.
events.why: TCP supplies the ports. IPv4 adds the source IP, destination IP, and TTL.

events.title: Look up the next hop
events.what: Next stop is 192.0.2.10.
events.why: A route picks the next stop. The IP destination stays the final computer.

events.title: Forward the packet
events.what: The router forwards the packet and lowers TTL to 63.
events.why: TTL is the packet’s hop budget. Lowering it at each router keeps packets from looping forever.

events.title: Hand the segment to TCP
events.raw: [Client] Ipv4.UnwrapPacket protocol=6 -> deliver enclosed segment to TCP
events.what: Client opens the IPv4 packet and takes out the TCP segment.
events.why: Protocol number 6 tells IPv4 that the payload belongs to TCP.

events.title: Process the incoming segment
events.what: Client TCP reads the ports, flags, and sequence numbers.
events.why: TCP uses control flags and sequence numbers to update the connection.

events.title: Advance the acknowledgment
events.raw: [Client] TCP peer expects byte sequence 1001 next.
events.what: The peer now expects sequence 1001.
events.why: An ACK names the next sequence number expected. It acknowledges what came before that number.

events.title: Update TCP state
events.what: Client changes its TCP state to Connected.
events.why: This endpoint has accepted its peer’s starting sequence number and considers the connection open.

events.title: Create a TCP segment
events.what: Client makes a ACK control segment.
events.why: This ACK names the next sequence number the sender expects to receive.

events.raw: [Server] TCP peer expects byte sequence 5001 next.
events.what: The peer now expects sequence 5001.
events.why: An ACK names the next sequence number expected. It acknowledges what came before that number.

events.title: Update TCP state
events.what: Server changes its TCP state to Connected.
events.why: This endpoint has accepted its peer’s starting sequence number and considers the connection open.

events.title: Queue the completed connection
events.raw: [Server kernel] Handshake complete. Queue connection for Accept().
events.what: The server OS puts the finished connection in its accept queue.
events.why: The final ACK has arrived. The connection is ready for the server app to pick up.

events.title: Return from Connect
events.what: Connect() returns to the browser.
events.why: The handshake is done in this model. The browser can now send its HTTP bytes.

events.title: Return a connected socket
events.raw: [Server socket] Accept() -> new connected socket for 192.0.2.10:51000
events.what: Accept() gives the server app a new socket for this client.
events.why: The listening socket keeps waiting for new clients. This connected socket carries the HTTP bytes.

events.title: Ask for buffered bytes

events.what: Server app calls Receive() with a buffer.
events.why: The app asks the OS to copy bytes that TCP has already put in order.

events.title: Copy bytes into the app
events.what: TCP copies 49 bytes into the app’s buffer.
events.why: Receive() returns the number copied. Any extra bytes stay in TCP’s buffer.

events.title: Build the HTTP response

events.why: 200 OK means the request succeeded. Content-Length gives the body’s size in bytes.
